title: Never going to New York to sing; Buddy held her back; Spivey's record company
summary: She says Buddy would not let her pursue a New York career, that he was mean to her, and compares Spivey, who had Lenny Kunstadt behind her.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Did you ever have any offers to go to New York, you know, like in the '30s or '40s or '50s, to go to New York and sing and stay there? Did you ever have any offers like that?
No, I didn't because (unintelligible).
He wouldn't let you go.
No, if he got ________, I would never have got it.
Oh, I see. Would you like to have gone?
I would have gone and I never would have come back.
Is that so? But you loved Buddy so much, you told me.
I loved him, but a lot of times I wished I never had seen him.
Is that because you would have liked to have had your career more -- your career as a singer?
Ronny can tell you, Ron know that man was very mean, ______. He was very mean to me. He was very mean. He told me in my own ______, told me to ______. I said, 'You got to be kidding.'
Ms. Wallace, if you would have been able to have more career, you know, to keep going more on, you know, in clubs and making records, would you have liked that?
I would have.
You would have?
Uh-huh.
You would have wanted that?
(Unintelligible).
Well, what do you think of the fact that Victoria made her own record company? What do you think of that?
That was all right, until she died.
But that was a very courageous thing to do, don't you think, to make her own record company?
Well, she had a man. I ain't got no man.
You mean Lenny Kunstat (PHONETIC)?
Yeah.
Yeah, he helped her a lot.
Yeah, (unintelligible), you know.
